content.text:
**I would not put Google display ads on Kuchup, and I would not buy Google Search ads for it yet either.** The site is already built as a conversion product, not as a place that sells attention.

Two different products get called “Google Ads.” They fail here for different reasons.

## Ads *on* the site (AdSense / display)

This fights the product you already have.

The public `/jobs/<slug>` pages are not a blog. They exist so Google and LinkedIn can land a visa-seeking engineer, then the primary CTA is Google OAuth → save to looking-to-apply → company workspace → credits / $29 Full Access. Display units on those pages would bid on the same intent: Indeed, StepStone, Relocate.me, LinkedIn. You would be paying Google a cut to walk people off the page you spent the wrapping funnel to get them onto.

The signed-in board is worse. That surface is a workspace. Ads next to “looking to apply” / MCP / upgrade CTAs look like a content farm and they compete with the only revenue model that already exists (credit packs and Full Access).

There is also a policy/quality problem. AdSense likes original, page-view media. Kuchup’s public listings are thin, frequently 410’d ATS copies with `hiringOrganization: Kuchup`. That is a good SEO/wrapping tactic and a bad AdSense site. Approval is not guaranteed, and even if it lands, RPMs on early job traffic are usually noise next to a $29 conversion.

Brand matters here more than on a recipe site. The buyer is an international engineer deciding whether to trust you with a visa search and a CV. Ad clutter is a trust tax.

## Ads *for* the site (Search / Performance Max)

The economics do not work until the funnel is measured.

“Visa sponsorship jobs Germany” and cousins are some of the most expensive job-seeker keywords on the internet. Your current paid ceiling is roughly **$29 once**, plus small credit packs. A $8–$40 click against that LTV is how you burn a wallet.

You also have no measurement layer in the product today — no gtag / GA4 / Ads conversion tags in the repo — so you could not even tell a cheap click from a paying one.

The acquisition path you already designed is better than Search ads at this stage: public JobPosting pages, `/sitemap-jobs.xml`, LinkedIn wrapping, country pages. That is high-intent traffic that lands on a save CTA instead of a bid auction.

If you ever buy Google Ads, start tiny and only after conversion tracking exists:

1. **Brand terms** (`kuchup`) — cheap insurance once people search the name.
2. A handful of **long-tail** queries (“visa sponsorship backend germany greenhouse”) with a hard CPA cap, landing on `/jobs` or a country page, converting on **save / signup**, not “visited homepage.”
3. Never Performance Max until that is proven. It will spend on generic job traffic.

I would not do even that until Search Console shows the job URLs actually getting impressions. Paid search in front of an unindexed wrapping funnel is guessing.

## How I would think about “ads” on this product

The high-value ad analog is **employer money**, not Google’s network. A company paying to be more visible among visa-positive roles is aligned: the user still wants a job, the payer is the company, you are not renting the page to a competitor. That is a later business, not a snippet to drop in this week.

If the question is “we need some revenue from anonymous browsers,” protect the job-page CTA and keep selling credits / Full Access. A few dollars of AdSense on a save page is the wrong trade.

**Short version:** treat Google as a crawler and a login provider, not as a publisher or a customer-acquisition channel, until organic job URLs and the $29 conversion are clearly working.
